s3.p2: Just like ![ico-20 ambulance], a function can move from one object to another (from where it is called).
s3.p3: In this context, the objects that call the function constitute the **call context**.
s3.p4: The function itself must have the ‘tools’ to carry out its task within the call context.
s3.p5: All these tools, which do not belong to the call context but are exclusively at the function’s disposal, belong to the **execution context**.
s3.p6: So, where will the ![ico-20 ambulance] go? That is the **call context**.
s3.p7: What is inside the ![ico-20 ambulance] is the **execution context**.

s6.p1: ![ico-20 warn] Every function call results in the creation of a new execution context.
s6.p2: The execution context is created before the code begins to run.
s6.p3: Each return (**⟦f21⟧**) exits the execution context.
s6.p4: Until the function has finished executing, its context will remain active.
s6.p5: As functions can call one another, their context is placed on a stack.
s6.p7: The top of this stack will always be the current execution context.
s6.p8: So what will be in this context?
s6.p10: ^^When a function is called, it is activated.^^
s6.p11: ^^It needs somewhere safe to ‘store’ the data it will be working with.^^
s6.p12: ^^In addition to the arguments it receives when called, it may have its own internal data, which is needed for the temporary storage of intermediate calculation results.^^
s6.p13: When a function is called, an object is created containing all the necessary variables.
s6.p14: In the language specification, this object is called **⟦f22⟧.**
s6.p15: ⟦f23⟧ contains the function’s arguments and all variables declared within the function (including functions).
s6.p16: ^^It is therefore also referred to as a _variable object_ or an _activation object_.^^
s6.p17: ^^Thus, the activation object can be likened to a locker for storing the function’s ‘personal belongings’.^^
s6.p18: ^^![ico-20 warn] It is not possible to access the activation object.^^
s6.p19: So, after a function is called:
s6.p25: ![ico-20 warn] Please note that all internal variables and nested functions are declared before the code begins to execute, regardless of the order in which they appear in the code.
s6.p26: ![ico-20 warn] However, variables are assigned values when the code begins to execute.
s6.p27: This leads to the **hoisting** of variable and function declarations.
s6.p28: ^^Although the variable declarations **_⟦f24⟧_** and **_⟦f25⟧_** appear in the code after the ⟦f21⟧ statement, when the execution context is formed in the first stage, an activation object (Lexical Environment) will be created, and all variables declared within the function will be included in this object.^^
s6.p29: ^^Thus, the declaration of the variables **_⟦f24⟧_** and **_⟦f25⟧_** will be ‘hoisted’ (it will take place before the function’s code begins to execute).^^
s6.p30: ^^However, value assignment takes place during the second phase, and the code will be executed sequentially, that is, at the time the code is executed.^^
s6.p31: ^^The value of the variable **_⟦f24⟧_** will not yet have been determined, so the console will display ⟦f26⟧.^^
s6.p32: ^^Similarly, at the time the code is executed^^
s6.p33: ^^the value of the variable  **_⟦f24⟧_**  will be  ⟦f26⟧, so the result of the assignment operation will be  **⟦f27⟧**,  which is what the code will output to the console.^^
s6.p34: ^^After that, the code will be executed^^
s6.p35: ^^The variables **_⟦f24⟧_** and **_⟦f25⟧_** will be assigned values.^^
s6.p36: ^^Therefore, the function will return the value **25**.^^
s6.p38: ^^will not take place, as the execution context will be exited before this code is reached.^^
s6.p39: ^^In this case, the declaration of the function  **⟦f28⟧**  will be included in the _Lexical Environment_ of the function  **⟦f29⟧** during the creation of its execution context, and will not affect the variable  **⟦f28⟧**,  which is declared in the global context.^^
s6.p40: ^^These will be different variables,  even though their identifiers are the same.^^
s7.p1: Scope (**⟦f30⟧**) limits the scope of variable and function identifiers.

s7.p5: ^^whilst the girl Sasha 🙎 is in the second^^
s7.p6: ^^There is an observer in each room^^
s7.p7: ^^If we ask the observer in the first room: ^^
s7.p10: ^^Let’s ask a similar question to an observer in the second room, ^^
s7.p12: ^^This is because each room has its own scope^^
s7.p13: ^^However, the scope of nested functions will be slightly different^^
s7.p14: ^^Let’s imagine that nested functions are boxes with tinted glass walls^^
s7.p15: ^^Our box-like functions are nested one inside the other, like matryoshka dolls: ^^
s7.p16: ^^the second box is inside the first,^^
s7.p17: ^^the third is inside the second, and so on...^^
s7.p18: ^^An observer in box 2 will see not only the contents of box 2, ^^
s7.p20: ^^and the room in which all the boxes are located^^
s7.p21: ^^but they cannot see the contents of box 3, ^^
s7.p22: ^^although the observer in box 3 can see it perfectly well... ^^
s7.p23: ^^as can the observers in all the other boxes ^^
s7.p25: ^^Thus, if there is a reference to a variable inside a function, the function will first look for that variable in its own ‘locker’, and if it cannot find it, it will not hesitate to ‘borrow’ that variable from the external locker in which it is located^^
s7.p26: ^^![ico-20 warn] All the ‘lockers’ belonging to others that are accessible to it constitute ![ico-20 pin] **_a chain of scopes_** of the function, which forms part of its ![ico-20 pin] **execution context**.^^
s7.p27: ^^The variable **⟦f31⟧** is declared in the global scope, in which the function **⟦f32⟧** is also declared.^^
s7.p28: ^^When the variable **⟦f31⟧** is declared, it is assigned the value 1.^^
s7.p29: ^^Since within the function **⟦f31⟧** there is no declaration of the variable **⟦f32⟧**, this variable is not included in the activation object (“locker”) of the function **⟦f32⟧** when the execution context of **⟦f32⟧** is formed.^^
s7.p32: ^^The function **⟦f32⟧**, having found no such variable in its own ‘locker’, looks to the outer ‘locker’, where such a variable does exist, and it is this variable that will be assigned the value 10.^^
s7.p33: ^^Thus, for each execution context, there is a distinct  visibility chain.^^
s7.p34: ^^The scope chain includes the scopes of all previous contexts on the stack.^^
s7.p36: ^^This example demonstrates how the **hoisting** mechanism works.^^
s7.p37: ^^The variable **⟦f31⟧** is declared in the global scope and assigned the value 1.^^
s7.p38: ^^Inside the body of the function **⟦f33⟧**, after the return statement, the function **⟦f31⟧** is declared.^^
s7.p39: ^^At first glance, when the code is executed sequentially, this declaration should not take effect, as the ⟦f21⟧ statement appears earlier.^^
s7.p40: ^^However, all declarations are collected into an activation object before the code begins to execute.^^
s7.p41: ^^Therefore, by the time the code for the function **⟦f33⟧** begins to execute, the function **⟦f31⟧** will already have been declared and will be safely located within ⟦f23⟧ of the function **⟦f33⟧**.^^
s7.p42: ^^As a result, variable and function declarations are ‘promoted’ to the ‘parent’ scope (in our case, the ‘parent’ is the function **⟦f33⟧**).^^
s7.p43: ^^You can verify this by printing the variable **⟦f31⟧** to the console.^^
s7.p44: ^^Once the code of the function **⟦f33⟧** has finished executing, its context will be ‘unmounted’, and the global context—in which the variable **⟦f31⟧** has the value 1—will become active again.^^
s7.p45: ^^Here, too, the declaration of the function **⟦f34⟧** is brought up.^^
s7.p46: ^^However, the function  **⟦f34⟧**  overrides the value of the variable  **⟦f31⟧**.^^
s7.p47: ^^In the context of the execution of the function  **⟦f33⟧**, at the moment the variable **⟦f31⟧** is assigned the value 5, there is no other declared variable **⟦f31⟧** apart from the function  **⟦f34⟧** itself.^^
s7.p48: ^^Thus, before the function  **⟦f34⟧** is called, the function will be printed to the console.^^
s7.p49: ^^After the function  **⟦f34⟧** is called, the new value (5) of the variable **⟦f31⟧** will be printed to the console.^^
s7.p50: ^^After that, the variable **⟦f31⟧** will be assigned a new value and the result (10) will be displayed in the console.^^
s7.p51: ^^When the function **⟦f33⟧** finishes executing and its context is ‘unmounted’, the global context will become active, in which the variable **⟦f31⟧** has the value 1.^^
s7.p52: ^^In this example, the function **⟦f34⟧** has redefined itself (it was a “function”, and has become a “number”).^^
s8.p1: So, a function may use variables that are not present in its ⟦f22⟧.
s8.p2: ^^These are external and are in a different context.^^
s8.p3: ^^But they are accessible to the function.^^
s8.p4: ^^The function ‘sees’ them, so they are within its _scope_.^^
s8.p5: ^^When a variable or function is referenced within a function, the engine will first look for that variable in the function’s ⟦f22⟧; if it is not found there, the search will continue along the scope chain.^^
s8.p6: ^^If the variable (or function) is not found, an exception ![ico-20 err] ⟦f35⟧ will be generated.^^
